title: Jenna Maroney you will always be famous! #OhMary #JaneKrakowski #30Ro...
transcript: So I saw Jane Krakowski's debut in oh, Mary last night, and it truly lived up to every single expectation that I had. As soon as this casting was announced, I bought tickets immediately because I knew I had to be there for her debut. It's one of those castings that, on paper, just feels so perfect. And it was. All of the Marys in O Mary have been very different from each other, and hers is certainly no exception. I think she's a little bit more subdued than a lot of the other Marys. She's not quite as shouty or manic, and very much brings her classic signature Jane Krakowski style of humor to the role. Her line delivery tends to be a little bit more matter of fact and blunt, and every line is delivered with a metaphorical wink and a smile, which is to say, she's very much playing to the audience, and the audience is eating it up. She also makes some truly wild choices, like reading Shakespeare in a Scottish accent for some reason. And of course, she throws in one of her classic 30 Rock lines for a bit of fan service. And then, of course, you have the Mad Cat medley. And I think this might be the best the Mad Cat medley has ever been sung. She absolutely knocks it out of the park. She is also joined by two other new cast members, including her 30 Rock co star Cheyenne Jackson. He plays Mary's teacher, and I also thought he was excellent. I won't spoil it just in case you haven't seen the show, but there is a twist with his character towards the end of the show. He makes a really interesting choice to really differentiate his portrayal pre twist and post twist that I thought worked really well. And then you have John Andrew Morrison as Lincoln, who is probably most well known for A strange loop, which played in the exact same theater. And he is a very different Lincoln than we have gotten before. He's much less serious than past iterations of the character, bringing a lot of energy and personality to the role. And I thought having a heightened Lincoln played really well off Jane's more subdued Mary. Don't get me wrong, Mary still very much the kooky one, but it still felt like a very fresh take on that dynamic, which I really appreciated.
